players.product: electroplating chemistry for advanced packaging & substrates (MacDermid Alpha)

quarterly_data.signal: Record 2025 (CFO): Q4 net sales increased 10% organically, led by high-end electronics growth primarily from AI and data center investments; Electronics segment organic growth was 13% with all 3 business verticals growing double digits; Q4 adjusted EBITDA $136 million, up 8% year-over-year in constant currency excluding divestitures, and 25.5% margin excluding pass-through metals. Full-year 2025 net sales $2.6 billion, growing 6% organically (Electronics 10% organic on AI and data center markets, advanced packaging metallization demand and new EV customers); adjusted EBITDA $548 million (26.5% margin ex pass-through metals); record adjusted EPS $1.49. The Q4 spike in silver and tin prices and related hedge losses cost several million dollars of adjusted EBITDA, a timing impact management expects to recapture in 2026; adjusted free cash flow was $256 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4: organic net sales 10%, Electronics organic 13%, adj. EBITDA $136 million, margin ex-metals 25.5%; FY2025: net sales $2.6 billion (6% organic), adj. EBITDA $548 million, adj. EPS $1.49

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 Electronics verticals (CFO): the Circuitry business has been a large beneficiary of AI-related investment because its market-leading pulse plating chemistry is used to fabricate high layer count server boards; Assembly Solutions grew 12% organically on consumer electronics and high-performance computing applications; Semiconductor Solutions grew 13% organically as advanced packaging applications drove demand for wafer-level plating chemistries and power electronics sales returned to growth on new customer wins.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 Assembly Solutions 12% organic; Semiconductor Solutions 13% organic

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2025 verticals (CFO): Assembly Solutions grew 8% organically, helped by rising demand for engineered preform materials used in high-performance computing; Circuitry Solutions grew 10% on high-performance computing and data center investment, with metallization solutions for dense high aspect ratio circuit boards suited to data centers; Semiconductor Solutions grew 13% (second consecutive year of mid-teens organic growth) on advanced packaging metallization and power electronics growth with new EV customers. Top ViaForm copper damascene customers grew 20% on average in 2025, a trend expected to continue in 2026; new product families are gaining traction, with growth opportunities in areas that intersect with printed circuit board metallization, such as IC substrate and large format panels. CEO: preforms keep chips flat on the highest-end server boards because the chips have gotten so big.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 Assembly 8%, Circuitry 10%, Semiconductor Solutions 13% organic; top ViaForm copper damascene customers grew 20% on average

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging exposure (CEO): products include wafer plating for the backside of wafers in packaging applications, advanced interconnect products for copper pillars and barrier layers, and chemistries for the highest-end printed circuit boards used in packages; wafer-level and advanced packaging sit at the center of its solution sets for foundries and OSATs. The dedicated wafer-level packaging business is about $150 million of revenue, now bumping up against $200 million with precious metal price increases (some precious metals there are not reported as pass-through); ancillary products bring total advanced packaging revenue to the multiple hundreds of millions.
quarterly_data.figure: wafer-level packaging about $150 million of revenue, bumping up against $200 million; advanced packaging revenue multiple hundreds of millions

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 guidance (CEO): adjusted EBITDA of $650 million to $670 million, including expected contributions from the EFC and Micromax acquisitions (roughly $70 million combined) and assuming current FX rates and metal prices, with a modest FX tailwind and a $5 million headwind from lapping the Graphics stub period, implying high single-digit organic adjusted EBITDA growth and adjusted EPS growth in the mid- to high teens. Market conditions are expected to resemble late 2025: continued strength in high-performance computing and leading-edge electronics, slower industrial markets, and top-line noise from metal prices. The Q1 guidance range is wider than usual because of January tin and silver price moves and acquisition seasonality. The company aims to outperform its end markets by 2 or 3 points through the cycle; in a bull case (data center strength continuing, a modestly better smartphone market) Electronics could keep growing organically at double digits, but the guide does not assume that.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 adj. EBITDA $650 million to $670 million; adj. EPS growth mid- to high teens; roughly $70 million acquisition contribution

quarterly_data.signal: Kuprion (CEO): the company made product qualification milestone payments in Q1 2026 and is in the final innings before ramping capacity at its first significant site in California; the pipeline of demand already exceeds the first site's production capacity, so a second site is being planned; the first plant should be ramped to full production in the second half of 2026, with guidance of multiple millions of dollars of revenue in '26 and a material EBITDA contribution in '27. Kuprion is not yet used in high-volume manufacturing anywhere; one application is Through-Glass Vias, the core layers for some of the highest-end printed circuit boards, where it solves a major customer pain point. 2025 capex advanced Kuprion and new advanced packaging product manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: multiple millions of dollars of revenue in '26; material EBITDA contribution in '27

quarterly_data.signal: New products and outgrowth (CEO): traction in power electronics, Kuprion, die attach solutions, circuit board fabrication and thermal materials drives part of the outgrowth versus the market, and the technology skews to the highest-end applications, such as the highest value circuit boards growing well in excess of the market. Argomax is broadening its customer base, with 20-plus percent growth in the back half of 2025 outside the original core customer, expected to continue; the power electronics business is "gaining share in excess of the automotive market".
quarterly_data.figure: Argomax 20-plus percent growth outside the original core customer in the back half of 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Market color (CEO): memory prices are rising because capacity is constrained by surging data center demand; this could hurt consumer electronics, but Element has more value on a high-end data center server board than in a PC or smartphone, and its 2026 forecast assumes quite strong data center growth but no strong smartphone or consumer electronics growth. The PCB baseline is Prismark: a 6% year in 2026 and a 9% CAGR from '24 to '29. Element is driven by board volume, not board dollar value, and growth is concentrated in high-value complex boards. For the past 3 years PCB square-meter growth has exceeded MSI growth; in 2025 PCB square meters grew high single digits versus Circuitry at 10%, and MSI grew mid-single digits versus Semi in the low teens, with similar outperformance expected in 2026. Activity in Asia in early January was described as unbelievable.
quarterly_data.figure: Prismark PCB baseline 6% in 2026; 9% CAGR from '24 to '29

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio (CFO/CEO): both acquisitions closed early in Q1 2026 for approximately $870 million, funded in part by a new $450 million term loan add-on; pro forma leverage is slightly above 3x and expected to approach 2.5x by year-end 2026. Micromax (advanced electronics inks and pastes plus low-temperature ceramic materials for satellites, EVs and data centers) had roughly $40 million of 2025 EBITDA and organic revenue growth north of 10%. EFC Gases & Advanced Materials (high-purity specialty gases and advanced materials, concentrated in semiconductor fabrication, electrical infrastructure and satellite propulsion, with a revenue CAGR above 15% since 2009 and recent growth mainly in semiconductor applications) had roughly $30 million and sits in the Specialty segment. Both are outperforming initial expectations. The slower-growth Graphics (flexographic printing) business was divested in Q1 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $870 million paid; Micromax roughly $40 million EBITDA in '25; EFC roughly $30 million
